Coalition losses grow! Valley colors with blood!

events.text: Coalition army loses courage in murderous fire.

events.title: Stone wagons!
events.text: Žižka has fodder wagons filled with stones and sends them hurtling down the slope—the enemy ranks shatter in the valley!

phases.name: Žižka's counterattack
phases.description: Žižka orders deadly counterattack down slope.

events.message: Žižka: "Now! Down the hill! For God's truth!"
Hussite cavalry and infantry rush down slope at disoriented enemy!

events.text: Attack from hill! +15% to Hussite units' attack.

phases.name: Coalition collapse
phases.description: Coalition army collapses. Rear units flee without fight.

events.message: Coalition collapses! Men flee toward Malešov!
Čeněk of Wartenberg: "Back! Everyone back!" Rear units didn't even enter battle.
1,200 coalition soldiers fell. Hussites lost only 200 men.
Žižka controls battlefield. Road to Kutná Hora open!

plzen.name: Siege of Plzeň

hussiteSide.strength: Combined field armies of Taborites and Orphans
hussiteSide.composition: Taborites, Orphans; reinforcements from Poland (Čapek of Sány)

enemySide.composition: Catholic Plzeň townsfolk, west-Bohemian Catholic nobility

plzen.terrain: The town ringed by ditches and a timber wall with nine towers; the Hussites had some 40 heavy bombards.

quotes.text: Ever after, the people of Plzeň bore a camel in their coat of arms.
quotes.source: J. Dolejší: Husité (on the town's arms)

trivia: Plzeň resisted the Hussites repeatedly (1421, 1427, 1431) and finally for 10 months in 1433-34 under Prokop Holý
Jan Čapek of Sány brought a camel back from the Polish campaign and led it before besieged Plzeň on October 11, 1433
The Plzeň men seized the camel in a sally - and put it in their coat of arms; after the siege they gave it to Nuremberg
The Hussites ringed the town with ditches and a timber wall of nine towers and 40 bombards
The siege was broken by hunger, exhaustion and TREASON - Přibík of Klenová called for the assault, then sabotaged it
The legate Palomar deliberately dragged out the Basel talks to break the Hussites from within
The failure at Plzeň dissolved the field armies and opened the road to the fratricidal Lipany
plzen.aftermath: The Hussites' greatest failure. The collapse of the field armies' unity led straight to Lipany.

sion.name: Siege of Sion Castle
sion.location: The little castle of Sion near Kutná Hora (~1 ha, no well)

enemySide.strength: The land levy plus Hungarian troops
enemySide.composition: The army of Sigismund of Luxembourg, Prague burghers

sion.terrain: A small new castle Roháč himself named "Sion". It had no well - the defenders suffered from thirst.

quotes.text: Like an exemplary warrior he did not give up his fight and would not submit.

trivia: Roháč named his new castle "Sion" himself - after the biblical holy mountain
The little castle was only about 1 hectare and had NO well - the defenders suffered from lack of water
The besieging commander Hynce Ptáček was Roháč's nephew - so at first he hesitated to attack
In late August Sigismund sent Hungarian reinforcements (Michal Országh), which hastened the assault
In Prague all were hanged by rank: Roháč on the highest gallows, the priest on the middle one, the brigands on the lowest
Archaeology questions the heroic version: only 3-4% war finds at the 4-month siege site - perhaps a "theatrical" siege where the kinsman Ptáček feigned the fighting
sion.aftermath: The last Hussite resistance was broken. Sigismund vengefully executed the defenders - and reportedly regretted it too late.
sion.reliability: Medium - archaeology tempers the chroniclers' image of a heroic slaughter

zatec.name: Defense of Žatec
zatec.location: Žatec - a promontory above the Ohře river, northwest Bohemia

hussiteSide.strength: Garrison of 5,400 foot and 400 horse + a mass of country folk
hussiteSide.composition: Town garrison; billmen, flailmen, crossbows and hook-guns

commanders: archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and Trier
enemySide.composition: The Second Crusade - imperial princes, cavalry, siege guns

zatec.terrain: A mighty fortress on a promontory encircled on three sides by the Ohře. Assault was possible from only one side.

quotes.text: Erkinger of Seinsheim made six assaults on Žatec with cannon and hook-guns, but failed to penetrate even the suburbs.
In the assault on Žatec, which had seemed to him an easy morsel, he was set upon by a strong body of defenders.

trivia: Žatec = the "Fortress of the Sun" (Tábor; Žatec-Sun, Louny-Moon, Slaný-Star)
SIX frontal assaults from September 19, 1421 were repelled
The whole town defended it: 5,400 foot, 400 horse and country folk
A bold sally from the gates on September 30 - the defenders cut down many and withdrew behind the walls
No defense commander survives in the record - the whole town held it
The siege broke on a false report that the Praguers were coming - the crusaders fled on October 2 and were pursued
A "blue pillar" reportedly stood over the burning camp - read as a divine omen
A year earlier Erkinger had thought Žatec "an easy morsel" - the defenders butchered him then

casualties.hussites: Low - the town was well provisioned
casualties.enemy: Considerable; plus hunger in the camp

zatec.aftermath: The Second Crusade fell apart without ever meeting Žižka in the field.

zivohost.name: Battle of Živohošť
zivohost.location: Area between Živohošť and Nový Knín

enemySide.composition: Heavy cavalry of Czech Catholic nobility

zivohost.terrain: High ground near Vltava crossing. Wagon fort was NOT used.
zivohost.outcome: Indecisive battle. Showed necessity of organized defense.
zivohost.aftermath: Indecisive battle. Showed necessity of organized defense.
zivohost.significance: Historically the FIRST major clash of the Hussite Wars. Demonstrated that pilgrims needed better organization and tactics.

quotes.text: Lord Peter rode with his squadron against the Ústí men, broke through them, and his entire cavalry squadron rode through them.

trivia: Historically the FIRST major clash of the Hussite Wars
Wagon fort was not used - it originated only later
Peter of Šternberk fell a year later at the Battle of Vyšehrad
Captured Hussites were thrown into Kutná Hora mine shafts

nekmir.name: Battle of Nekmíř
nekmir.location: Near Nekmíř fortress, 17 km NW of Plzeň

hussiteSide.composition: Infantry from Plzeň, wagons with guns and hand cannons

nekmir.terrain: Field near Nekmíř fortress. FIRST USE OF WAGON FORT in Hussite Wars.
nekmir.outcome: Hussite victory. Wagon tactics were born.
nekmir.aftermath: Hussite victory. Wagon tactics were born.
nekmir.significance: FIRST documented use of wagon fort in history. Only 7 wagons in semicircle formation proved the concept worked.

quotes.text: Žižka repelled him from the wagons and killed Hynek of Nekmíř. Then he continued his march and that night demolished three fortified strongholds.

trivia: FIRST documented use of wagon fort in history
Only 7 wagons - semicircle formation
Bohuslav of Švamberk later JOINED the Hussites!
Memorial to the first wagon fort at Nekmíř built only in 2017 - 598 years after the battle!
Žižka's 7 wagons were a demolition convoy (rams, guns, a trebuchet) - the wagon fort was IMPROVISED when he was ambushed on the road
The field toward Všeruby where Žižka drew the wagons together is still said to be called 'Na smrtelnici' - the place of death
The lords' cavalry attacked a wagon fort for the first time - they had no idea it could not simply be swept aside
nekmir.reliability: Low - only one source (Old Czech Annals)

sudomer.name: Battle of Sudoměř
sudomer.location: Between Markovec and Škaredý fishponds, 14 km from Strakonice

enemySide.composition: Heavy cavalry, Hospitallers, squires of landfrieden

sudomer.terrain: Narrow dam between fishponds - Markovec filled, Škaredý muddy. KEY FACTOR - mud trapped dismounted knights.
sudomer.outcome: Hussite victory. First great demonstration of wagon tactics.
sudomer.aftermath: Hussite victory. First great demonstration of wagon tactics.
sudomer.significance: Foundation of Žižka's reputation as undefeated commander. Proved wagon fort could defeat heavy cavalry.

quotes.text: ...on the day of the Annunciation of the Virgin Mary, Lord Břeněk of Švihov, Valkoun of Adlar, and Jan Žižka with other brothers...

trivia: Žižka was one-eyed and approximately 60 years old
LEGEND about veils of Hussite women blinding knights is Piccolomini's fabrication
Henry of Hradec mortally wounded by arrow TO THE THUMB
Foundation of Žižka's reputation as undefeatable commander

vitkov.name: Battle of Vítkov

hussiteSide.strength: 26 men, 2 women and a maiden in the blockhouses; Prague relief with flails
hussiteSide.composition: Flailmen and glaivemen, few crossbows (little gunpowder), 3 women

enemySide.strength: ~30,000 total; 7-8,000 in the sector, but only ~300 riders fit into the neck

vitkov.terrain: Extended ridge with steep slopes, wooden blockhouses. Narrow access path prevented use of numerical superiority.
vitkov.significance: Saved Prague from the First Crusade. Became symbol of Hussite resistance and Czech national memory.

quotes.text: And Žižka coming there would have been killed if his men had not pulled him with flails from the enemies' hands.
And the enemies seeing the sacrament and hearing the bell ringing and the mighty cry of the people, seized with tremendous fear took flight...

trivia: 3 WOMEN defended Vítkov
Battle cry 'Hrrr at them!' became Hussite motto
Equestrian statue of Žižka on Vítkov - third largest in the world
The day before, cavalry scattered Prague townsfolk who charged out against orders
The crusaders forgot their ladders — so they floundered in the ditches below the blockhouse
vitkov.reliability: High - Vavřinec of Březová was a contemporary chronicler

vysehrad.name: Battle under Vyšehrad
vysehrad.location: Pankrác Plain, area around St. Pankrác church

commanders: Hynek Krušina of Lichtenburg (25 years old)
hussiteSide.composition: Praguers, Orebites, Taborites, Žatec, Louny forces

enemySide.composition: Hungarians, Germans, Silesians, Czech Catholic nobility

vysehrad.terrain: Flat plain with side ravine to Podolí. Side ravine became trap for nobility.
vysehrad.outcome: Decisive victory - 'substantially greater than at Vítkov'. Collapse of royal party.
vysehrad.aftermath: Decisive victory - 'substantially greater than at Vítkov'. Collapse of royal party.
vysehrad.significance: Destroyed backbone of Czech Catholic nobility. 25 banner lords fell. Secured Prague for Hussites.

quotes.text: [The nobility] proudly informed the king that they would go into fire even where he himself certainly would not be.

trivia: 25 BANNER LORDS of Czech nobility fell
Vyšehrad garrison honored surrender agreement
Dead lay NAKED for 3 DAYS on battlefield
Sigismund came LATE - after 8:00, when garrison was to surrender
After the battle a pillar colored like a rainbow reportedly appeared at night over the field — read as an omen
vysehrad.reliability: High - multiple sources including Eberard Windecke

kutna_hora.name: Battle of Kutná Hora

enemySide.composition: Hungarian cavalry, German and Austrian detachments

kutna_hora.terrain: Hilly countryside, strategic Kaňk hill. Terrain enabled night escape.
kutna_hora.outcome: Hussite victory. Brilliant night breakthrough with wagon fort.
kutna_hora.aftermath: Hussite victory. Brilliant night breakthrough with wagon fort.
kutna_hora.significance: FIRST mobile artillery maneuver in history - night breakthrough. Proved blind Žižka's genius.

quotes.text: ...on the way they burned villages and raping virgins and women unto death, then murdered them...

trivia: Žižka was COMPLETELY BLIND - lost second eye during siege of Rábí
Kutná Hora citizens secretly cooperated with Sigismund and opened gates
Sigismund spent Christmas believing he won
FIRST mobile artillery maneuver in history - night breakthrough
Kutná Hora miners threw captured Hussites into mine shafts - hence the betrayal
Sigismund drove herds of oxen and cows at the Hussites ("the Horned Enemy") to frighten them - they first took them for devils, then herded them into the wagon fort as provisions
At Kutná Hora Sigismund lost over 5,000 men almost without a fight - sevenfold the losses at Vítkov
The blind Žižka was knighted on January 11, 1422 - he "won for the chalice even without sight"
Booty: 540 wagons full of goods, jewels and books ("one book was worth a fortune")

nemecky_brod.name: Battle of Německý Brod
nemecky_brod.terrain: Táborec hill by Habry and the frozen Sázava, bitter frost. Main fighting at the town walls (St. Adalbert suburb).
nemecky_brod.outcome: Crushing victory. 2nd Crusade ends in complete debacle.

casualties.enemy: Thousands dead in field + in city

nemecky_brod.aftermath: Crushing victory. 2nd Crusade ends in complete debacle.
nemecky_brod.significance: Avenged massacre of Hussites at Kutná Hora. 548 knights drowned under ice. City empty for years.

quotes.text: The town of Německý Brod falls and all perish... at least one thousand five hundred people.
[The massacre was] a great sin on the souls of all Hussites involved.

trivia: Žižka was ALLEGEDLY knighted at Německý Brod (around January 10)
Some 548 riders reportedly drowned under the Sázava ice - Dolejší does NOT dispute the ice; he counts them among the ~12,000 campaign losses, and his doubt targets the "seven years deserted" claim
City was EMPTY FOR YEARS - wolves ran through streets
Massacre was revenge for murder of Hussites at Kutná Hora
The real horror of the retreat was the frost - fleeing women and children froze to death on the road (Dolejší)
The crusaders made their stand backs to the walls by St. Adalbert church, covered by a Teutonic Knights commandery
Among the prisoners was Záviš Černý of Garbów - at the close of the fighting he most likely commanded the royal garrison in the town
The Táborec rise near Habry, where Pippo Scolari arrayed his troops for battle, is today called "Peklo" (Hell)
When the town was stormed on January 9, the women and maidens were led out unharmed - only then was it given to the flames

most.name: Battle of Most

enemySide.strength: Saxon army + Most militia + Catholic nobility

most.terrain: Slope of Hněvín hill with castle. Hussites attacked UPHILL without wagon fort - MISTAKE.
most.outcome: HUSSITE DEFEAT. Weakening of Jan Želivský's position.
most.aftermath: HUSSITE DEFEAT. Weakening of Jan Želivský's position.
most.significance: FIRST major Hussite defeat. Erased from textbooks - didn't fit image of invincible Hussites.

quotes.text: [Vavřinec of Březová provides description but was not Želivský supporter - may have exaggerated defeat]

trivia: FIRST major Hussite defeat
Erased from textbooks - didn't fit image of invincible Hussites
Virgin Mary became protector of Most
Žižka WAS NOT PRESENT - recovering from going blind
Before the battle the Hussites were already dividing spoils and underrated the German horse - the defeat came in confusion and a night flight

usti.name: Battle of Ústí nad Labem
usti.terrain: Gentle hill with plateau. Double line of wagon fort.
usti.significance: LAST BATTLE where cavalry frontally attacked wagon fort. Piccolomini wrongly attributed victory to dead Žižka.

quotes.text: And the stream which flows through Ústí was entirely thick and bloody from the great slaughter of men and horses.
Czechs should remember that the Lord God gave them victory at Ústí...

trivia: Piccolomini WRONGLY attributed victory to dead Žižka
FIRST great battle of Prokop the Great as commander
7 imperial counts and 23 bannerlords fell
Truce letter refused → both sides vowed to spare no one; 24 kneeling lords slain
LAST BATTLE where cavalry frontally attacked wagon fort
The Ruthenian prince Fedor of Ostrog also fought in the Hussite army - Ústí drew even foreign nobles

tachov.name: Battle of Tachov

enemySide.composition: FIRST use of own wagon fort by crusaders

tachov.terrain: Area around Stříbro and Tachov. Indecisive - crusaders fled.
tachov.outcome: Without battle - crusaders fled! 4th Crusade ends in debacle.
tachov.aftermath: Without battle - crusaders fled! 4th Crusade ends in debacle.
tachov.significance: Crusades halted for 4 years. Demonstrated complete demoralization of crusader armies.

quotes.text: And when the Taborites approached within three miles, said princes fled to Bavaria...
The cardinal tore down banners, threw them before Germans on ground and fiercely berated them.
I see not whom to flee from, I see no enemy!

trivia: Crusaders used own wagon fort - ineffective
Cardinal Beaufort recruited English archers only in 1429 - they never reached Bohemia, diverted to France
'I see not whom to flee from, I see no enemy!' - sarcastic remark by knight Kamrovec
Crusades halted for 4 years
The knight Kamrovec, author of the "I see no enemy" quip, fell storming Tachov in the breach - the spot is still called "the Bloody Lane"

nisa.name: Battle of Nysa (Silesia)
nisa.terrain: Before city walls. Surprise and rapid maneuver.
nisa.outcome: Crushing victory. Cities surrender or pay tribute.
nisa.aftermath: Crushing victory. Cities surrender or pay tribute.
nisa.significance: Part of first 'Beautiful Ride' into Silesia. Only major battle of Silesian raid - cities then surrendered without fight.

quotes.text: Some two thousand Silesians were slain or drowned in the river; the Czechs stormed the suburb and burned it with the enemy's own wagons.

trivia: Part of first 'BEAUTIFUL RIDE' into Silesia
Up to 2,000 Silesians killed or drowned in the Nysa river
Duke of Legnica-Brzeg cowardly fled
Only major battle of Silesian raid - cities then surrendered without fight
The tribute system began with a pact between the captains and the council of Münsterberg; non-payers were burned down (Falkenberg, Brzeg)
nisa.reliability: Low - less documented, most details reconstructed

domazlice.name: Battle of Domažlice
domazlice.location: Between Domažlice and Kdyně, at Baldov hill

hussiteSide.composition: Combined unions of Taborites, Orphans and Praguers

enemySide.composition: Several thousand wagons in Hussite style (9,000 planned), hundreds of guns

domazlice.terrain: Road to Domažlice, Všeruby pass. Pass - narrow bottleneck for fleeing.
domazlice.outcome: Legendary victory. End of military solution, negotiations at Basel Council.
domazlice.aftermath: Legendary victory. End of military solution, negotiations at Basel Council.
domazlice.significance: Peak of Hussite glory. Largest crusade fled without daring to fight. CARDINAL'S HAT lost in flight became symbol.

quotes.text: When that destructive nation approached us... seized with such horror we all in sudden dread; there our strength vanishes and counsel flees with hope...
...already resounded the clatter of wagon march and song of whole camp loudly Who are God's warriors...

trivia: CARDINAL'S HAT lost in flight - symbol of victory
Choral 'Ktož jsú boží bojovníci' sounded before battle
Cesarini later advocated diplomatic negotiation
Crusaders fled without daring to fight
The crusaders heard the chorale "Ye Who Are Warriors of God" from SEVEN KILOMETERS away - the Hussites were not even in sight
The cardinal Cesarini left behind loot: the papal bull, a gold pectoral, his hat and robe - kept in Domažlice for two centuries

lipany.name: Battle of Lipany
lipany.location: Between Hřiby and Lipská hora, 40 km E of Prague
lipany.terrain: Lipská hora (more advantageous for radicals), plain at Hřiby. TWO ARMIES IN WAGON FORTS facing each other.
lipany.outcome: Crushing defeat of radicals. End of field armies. Compactata at Jihlava 1436.
lipany.aftermath: Crushing defeat of radicals. End of field armies. Compactata at Jihlava 1436.
lipany.significance: End of radical Hussitism. Fratricidal battle where Hussites defeated Hussites. 'Czechs can be defeated only by Czechs.'

quotes.text: Up, up, at them, they're already fleeing!
quotes.source: Call of radicals - Bartošek of Drahonice

quotes.text: And there said lords pursued them so rapidly still striking them that they ran between their wagons and right there on wagons killed both priests Prokop...
Czechs can be defeated only by Czechs.
Who stops here, ponder where leads discord of nation.

trivia: George of Poděbrady (future king) participated at 14 years
~700 prisoners; by chronicle tradition some burned in barns (the radio history reports only capture)
Body of Prokop the Great NEVER FOUND
Jan Roháč of Dubá resisted until 1437 - then executed
lipany.reliability: High - many sources including Bartošek of Drahonice

horice.name: Battle of Hořice
horice.location: Gothard hill (357 m), SE of Hořice in Jičín region

enemySide.composition: Cavalry formations of Catholic Czech nobility

horice.terrain: Gothard hill. Wagon fort on hilltop.
horice.outcome: Crushing Orebite victory. Showed strength of eastern Bohemian Hussites.
horice.aftermath: Crushing Orebite victory. Showed strength of eastern Bohemian Hussites.
horice.significance: FIRST INTERNAL CONFLICT OF HUSSITES. Eastern Bohemia = cradle of Hussite commanders.

quotes.text: When Žižka rode close to them near Hořice, he attacked them... that he captured several hundred of them.
Lord Čeněk with some lords gathered against Žižka and they had battle together and there Žižka defeated those lords, captured and killed many of them.

trivia: Čeněk of Wartenberg - notorious TURNCOAT (changed sides 4-5 times)
Diviš Bořek of Miletínek - later victor at Lipany
FIRST INTERNAL CONFLICT OF HUSSITES
Eastern Bohemia = cradle of Hussite commanders
After the victory Žižka took the fortress of Kozojedy and had sixty people burned there
Before the campaign Žižka exhorted them: "Remember our first fight - few against many, unarmoured against the armoured, you fought bravely!"

malesov.name: Battle of Malešov
malesov.location: At Malešov fortress, 6 km S of Kutná Hora, valley of Bohynka stream

enemySide.composition: Prague union + Plzeň landfrieden + moderate Utraquists

malesov.terrain: Valley at Malešov - narrow passage. Žižka blocked passage with wagon fort.
malesov.outcome: Brilliant victory of blind commander. BLOODIEST battle of Hussite Wars.

casualties.enemy: ~1,400 fallen on both sides (326 of them Prague householders)

malesov.aftermath: Brilliant victory of blind commander. BLOODIEST battle of Hussite Wars.
malesov.significance: Peak of Žižka's career - blind defeated superior numbers. Coalition attempted ASSASSINATION of Žižka. Žižka died 4 months later (October 11, 1424).

quotes.text: Item, Praguers shat themselves with wheat at Malešov, for all Praguers were girded with wheat as sign.
...Žižka entered the valley because he knew that it is a gorge in which enemies absolutely cannot deploy their ranks... killed 3,000 Praguers...
In the year of Our Lord 1424 Žižka with his men defeated Praguers in battle and took from them many wagons with guns; three hundred Prague citizens fell.

trivia: WAGONS WITH STONES - legend or reality? Predecessor of tank tactics
Peak of Žižka's career - blind defeated superior numbers
Coalition attempted ASSASSINATION of Žižka
Žižka died 4 months later (October 11, 1424)
The standard-bearer Turkovec fell with the Prague banner in hand; among the dead was also Žižka's son-in-law
malesov.reliability: Medium - precise location of battlefield not determined
